images.caption: Figure 1:Conventional computer-use agents execute tasks through fixed, human-designed interfaces. Agent S4 evolves interfaces as software repositories through experience. A task agent attempts synthetic tasks, and a meta-agent studies its trajectories to construct and refine the repositories. Each repository combines interfaces, such as GUI interactions, file operations and application-specific workflows, with knowledge of when to use them.

Figure 3:Agent S4 turns task experience into an evolving repository of interfaces and knowledge.Starting from parents selected by held-out validation, the meta-agent
studies their task trajectories to identify limitations, then revises one
repository through mutation or combines ideas from two through crossover.
Task agents then use the descendant to produce trajectories on synthetic
tasks and a separate score on held-out validation tasks. Each descendant
joins the population alongside its parents, allowing earlier designs to be
revisited and recombined over successive iterations.

Figure 5:Human-curated versus Evolved Interface. Top: the Qwen CUA baseline uses a fixed, human-designed interface prioritizing frequent screenshots with mouse and keyboard actions. It reads the receipts and searches the card charges through repeated GUI interactions (steps 21–111).
Bottom: Prime Agent with the repository evolved by Agent S4. It reads the mailbox and the bank records through the evolvedbrowserinterface, whosebrowser.apisends requests from inside the already logged-in tab and returns the data as text (calls 17 and 44). It fetches the attachments withcurl, and reads them withpdftotext.

Figure 9:How the task agent uses an evolved repository.(a)On an
OSWorld V2 task, the task agent lists the available interfaces, reads the
usage notes of one and calls it from its code. Outputs are shortened.(b)The repository selected without a scratch VM
(Table2) is a Python package. Each interface is a
module of functions whose docstrings say how and when to use them, including
lessons from earlier trajectories. Docstrings are shortened.run_batch,apiand thelofilemodule were added
during evolution.

Figure 10:Reusable browser helpers expose the instructions needed
for the rest of the task.Cropped frame from the evolved task-046
recording showing the TeamChat direct message. It asks the agent to
check payments and deliver photos or previews accordingly. The box
abbreviates the helper names and arguments passed through the CLI in
tool cell 11. The frame illustrates the page content; operation timing
is measured from the trajectory, independently of the recording.

Figure 12:Reading a mailbox in MailHub(s_010). The seed agent reads the case
emails through the GUI in 60 calls (8–67). Its first six clicks land above
the email list because it uses coordinates from its 1200-pixel screenshots as
screen coordinates. A click meant for the inbox opens Starred, and its attempt
to read the page from code is refused with403 Forbidden. Withif-011,page_textlists the inbox and onecdp_evalcall fetches the mailbox with full email bodies inside the
logged-in tab, in 12 calls and without a screenshot.

Figure 13:Exporting an XMind map(s_005). The seed agent tries to export
a PNG through XMind’s menus in calls 249–299. Its click on the Export
submenu lands between PNG and JPEG, and an “Export to JPEG” panel opens.
Its clicks on Cancel miss, and the episode ends at the call limit without an
image. Withif-029from a separate evolution run, the agent builds
the map withxmind.build_mapandsave_map, and one call
toxmind.render_pngwrites the image.

Figure 14:Reading a Zotero library(s_007). The seed agent checks items and
notes through the GUI in 42 calls (59–100). Nine clicks meant for the Cancel
button of a plugin dialog miss (calls 61–79), and the agent closes the
dialog with an Escape key press at call 82. Later it clicks outside the
screen and asks a vision model to locate the Notes tab. Withif-029from a separate evolution run,zotero.list_collectionsandlist_itemsreturn the library as data in one call. The interface
covers reading only: on this build the API rejects writes.

Figure 15:Submitting a review in ReviewSphere(s_022). The seed agent’s clicks meant
to close two popups open a software-store window, and its click on Write
Review misses until it rescales the coordinates. It then writes its own
Chrome client to fill the form; Chrome first refuses the connection with403 Forbidden, and the form is filled at call 37. Withif-026from a separate evolution run, calls 5–26 read the page,
open the form, fill six fields, check them, and submit, mostly throughbrowser.chrome_js, with no failed calls.

Figure 16:Resolving tracked changes in a Word document(s_026). The seed agent reads the raw
document XML and rebuilds insertion and deletion elements by hand in calls
17–28; its comments XML fails to parse at call 24. Withif-030from a separate evolution run, the agent lists the changes withredline_list, then accepts eight and rejects six withaccept_redlinesandreject_redlinesin one call.

Figure 17:Accessing a TeamChat tab(OSWorld V2 task038). The bare agent repeatedly clicks the
MailHub tab while trying to activate TeamChat, then hits TeamChat’s close
control. Withif-024, call 14 usesbrowser.chrome_cdpwith a tab ID to read the general-channel rules without switching tabs
through the screen. Later pinned-rule checks and CRM updates remain.
The full episodes take 94 and 95 model steps and receive task scores of
0.6517 and 0.70, respectively.

Figure 18:Plotting a function in KAlgebra(KAlgebra:A-02). The seed agent’s Add click lands in the graph,
and repeated clicks target the color control instead of the expression
input. It eventually finds the input and plotsy=ln⁡(x)2y=\ln(x)^{2}in
calls 64–67. Withif-016, call 8 usesrest.kalgebra_add_2dto add the curve andrest.kalgebra_functions_2dto read it back; call 10 shows
the resulting plot. Both episodes pass, in 68 and 11 model steps,
respectively.

Figure 19:Storing a calculation in KAlgebra(KAlgebra:C-01). The seed agent repeatedly clicks above the
calculator input and sends test characters before correcting the
coordinates and storinglog2⁡(3)\log_{2}(3)inp. Withif-016,kalgebra.evaluate_linesenters the expression through the GUI
and checks the variable. Its first attempt reportspmissing;
the agent selects the Calculator tab and retries, confirmingp=1.58496250072at call 17. Both episodes pass, in 40 and
21 model steps, respectively.

Figure 20:Computing raster statistics in GRASS GIS(GrassGIS:B-12). The seed agent locates the GUI console,
corrects its typing method, and retries Return until it focuses the
command input and obtains the statistics. Withif-016, call 8
runsr.univar map=lakesthroughgrass.grass_runagainst the live mapset and returns the statistics as text, includingn=263975andsum=263975. The evolved agent also runs
the command through the GUI in calls 15–18. Both episodes pass, in
40 and 21 model steps, respectively.
